principles: Use one consistent lifecycle policy for code and documentation audits.
Avoid special-case review friction unless risk evidence justifies it.
Keep degraded 3x1 honest and visibly lower assurance.
Separate documentation policy changes from runtime implementation.
drivers: User explicitly wants document audit to follow ordinary automatic 3x2/3x1 rules.
The previous always-on decision-doc rule conflicts with that direction.
Implementation still needs a later code change, so the plan must state the transition honestly.

options.name: A: Keep decision-doc always-on 3x2
pros: Maximum review strictness for governance docs
cons: Can block documentation audits even when review found no meaningful risk

options.name: B: Treat document audits like ordinary development automatic escalation
pros: One consistent rule for code and docs
Escalates only when first review reveals two or more countable problems
Can use the same explicit degraded 3x1 fallback semantics
cons: Requires follow-up implementation to replace current decision-doc special case
Default documentation changes receive less mandatory quorum than the old policy

chosen: B: Treat document audits like ordinary development automatic escalation
rationale: Choose B because the user explicitly clarified that documentation audit should follow ordinary development automatic 3x2/3x1. The plan should stop preserving always-on decision-doc 3x2 as the desired future rule, while noting current code remains legacy until implementation changes it.

preMortem.scenario: The document implies the current runtime already changed.
preMortem.trigger: The plan removes always-on wording without a transition note.
preMortem.consequence: Operators expect DONE behavior that is not implemented yet.
preMortem.mitigation: Add explicit current-vs-target wording that current code may still enforce legacy decision-doc quorum until implementation lands.

preMortem.trigger: The automatic trigger is vague or omitted for docs.
preMortem.consequence: Risky decision docs pass with ordinary review despite substantial first-round issues.
preMortem.mitigation: State docs use the same first REVIEW round countable-problem threshold and same degraded fallback restrictions.

preMortem.scenario: 3x1 fallback is treated as full documentation approval.
preMortem.trigger: Audit wording says document audit can use 3x1 without lower-assurance labels.
preMortem.consequence: Future implementation silently downgrades review quality.
preMortem.mitigation: Reuse degraded-single-host terminology and assurance fields from B-d959.
